extraction.name: Video-MME
extraction.description: Video-MME is the first-ever comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark crafted for MLLMs in Video analysis. The dataset comprises 900 videos across various scenarios with 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions (3 per video). It spans 6 visual domains including Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual, with 30 fine-grained categories. Videos vary significantly in length, ranging from 11 seconds to 1 hour, evaluating adaptability across varying temporal contexts. The benchmark incorporates associated subtitles and audio tracks for enhanced multimodal analysis.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The construction of the Video-MME dataset involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Videos are collected from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 finely-grained video categories. For each category, videos with varying duration lengths are collected, including short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long videos (30-60 minutes). Corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios are also obtained. The resulting dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos are sourced from YouTube. A domain hierarchy is established for sourcing, identifying 6 key domains: Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Life Record, and Multilingual, informed by popular trends on YouTube. Each domain is further subdivided into specific tags, yielding a total of 30 finely-grained video categories.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Frame extraction is performed by uniformly sampling a specified number of frames from the video. For Gemini 1.5 Pro, frames are sampled at 1 frame per second for short and medium videos, and at 1 frame every 2 seconds for long videos. For other models, frame extraction adheres to their respective official guidelines. In the subtitle-enabled setting, subtitles corresponding to the timestamps of the sampled video frames are selected to ensure accurate coherent synchronization between visual and textual multimodal input.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Following the collection of raw video data, videos are annotated with high-quality question-answer (QA) pairs using a multiple-choice QA format. Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning are recruited. Each annotator is tasked with thoroughly viewing the entire video, then iteratively creating three relevant questions, each accompanied by four candidate options, contributing to a total of 2,700 QA pairs. These questions encompass 12 distinct task types, including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Each QA pair is designed to be closely tied to the video content, preventing MLLMs from answering accurately without directly referencing the video.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: To guarantee the quality of the dataset, a rigorous manual review process is conducted. Each QA pair undergoes examination by a different annotator to verify that (i) the language expression is clear and precise; (ii) the question is answerable with logically consistent candidate options, and the designated correct answer is appropriate. To ensure that questions are sufficiently challenging and require video content as a critical clue to answer, text-only questions are provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro and QA pairs that can be answered solely based on textual questions are filtered out. Questions that do not meet this criterion are returned to the original annotator for revision. Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup, underscoring the robustness of the video content-based requirement.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro (used for quality filtering to ensure questions require video content)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: A general decline in MLLM performance is observed as video duration increases for all models. This trend suggests that limitations in processing longer video sequences could be a critical bottleneck in the performance of MLLMs. For open-source models, the restricted input frames can become an information bottleneck for understanding the full content of long videos. The certificate length analysis reveals that medium and long video subsets require much longer video content digestion to answer questions, making Video-MME the most challenging Video QA dataset to date.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Video-MME is designed for evaluating MLLMs' performance in video understanding tasks. The benchmark is available to both video-specific models and advanced image-based models by extending their input to multi-frame images. Use cases include: Testing and evaluation of multimodal large language models on video analysis tasks including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis across varying temporal contexts (short, medium, and long videos). The benchmark enables comprehensive evaluation of temporal understanding capabilities.
